speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) how will Punggol residents' safety be prioritised when autonomous vehicles (AV) are trialed in the fourth quarter of 2025; (b) how does the Ministry ensure that rides offered by AVs are affordable and accessible to residents; and (c) how will the Ministry involve public transport workers and ensure they have a role to play when AVs are rolled out.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) what key performance indicators will be used to measure the success of autonomous vehicle trials; (b) what safety benchmarks are in place; and (b) how legal liability and system security risks will be addressed.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) what system-level benefits such as (i) improved accessibility (ii) reliability of public transport and (iii) congestion and emissions reductions, Singapore anticipates from autonomous vehicle (AV) deployment; and (b) whether such efficiencies may enable more affordable public transport in the future.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
text: asked the Acting Minister for Transport (a) how will the Government’s autonomous vehicle (AV) strategy affect driving-related jobs; (b) what new job opportunities are expected; and (c) how the Ministry plans to support workers in transitioning to AV-related roles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Autonomous vehicles (AVs) can enhance connectivity and create good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVs will add to our public transport network without running up against fundamental manpower constraints.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will start by deploying autonomous shuttles to operate scheduled, fixed-route services within our towns.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These shuttle services can directly connect residents to key transport nodes and amenities such as the market and polyclinic.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: If successful, we intend to expand the service to other towns that are further away from the city, such as Tengah.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) have put in place safeguards to ensure safe AV deployment in the regulatory sandbox as provided for in the Road Traffic Act.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The vehicle must be able to respond safely to the behaviour of other road users and adhere to traffic rules.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For a start, a safety operator will be on board the AV at all times.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All AVs deployed on roads must have third-party liability insurance, covering death, bodily injury and property damage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Third parties would be compensated in the event of accidents, similar to conventional vehicles.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The AV industry will bring new job opportunities for Singaporeans, including for our transport workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There will be roles such as safety operators, remote operators, engineers and technicians.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Government and AV operators will roll out training and reskilling programmes to help drivers to take on opportunities in the AV sector, or to move into other sectors if they prefer.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will put these programmes in place early to provide drivers with options and time to go for reskilling.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: I declare I am the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: The announcement of the roll-out of the AV shuttle trials in Punggol has been met with both excitement and curiosity.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: This will no doubt allow our Punggol residents to be familiarised with the technology and services, and to be more confident of the use of AVs in their daily commute.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: What are the safety key performance indicators to be achieved during the non-passenger phase of the Punggol AV trials before graduating into passenger services?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: And will there be a town-wide consultation with Punggol residents during the various roll-out phases?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: In addition, I note that there has been some identification of new jobs that would be created with AV trials, such as safety drivers and remote operators which the Senior Minister of State has talked about.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
text: How will the Ministry direct the appointed AV service providers to work with the transport unions and associations on prioritising these jobs for existing transport workers and to make more accessible the application for such jobs to a wider group of transport workers?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She has been a very, very active proponent for workers in the transport industry – in particular, after we have shared about our AV plans.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First and foremost, safety is a key priority for MOT and LTA.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is why we are taking a phased approach to deploy the use of AV services.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They are subject to LTA's AV assessment framework, which requires them to pass a closed-circuit test at the Centre of Excellence for Testing and Research of Autonomous Vehicles (CETRAN).

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: All shuttles are also monitored in real-time with performance data collected and analysed to ensure safe and reliable operations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Apart from that, when we first identified the routes for trial in Punggol, we have taken care to identify what we call as "PUDOs", pick up and drop-off points, where there is adequate safety distance for onboarding as well as disembarking of commuters.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, we are looking forward to having a bigger and engagement, a more widespread engagement with residents in Punggol, in particular those who go to the preschools, the schools as well as Active Ageing Centres to sensitise them to the use of the AVs on the roads.
Just very broadly, at this point in time, we see that there are potential new job roles in the ecosystem relevant to AV operators.
These would be, for instance, in the areas of engineering and software development, depot operations, vehicle and fleet operations.
There are also potential roles with the AV tech providers in the areas of software development, cyber security and compliance.
And lastly, for enablers of the AV ecosystem, such as, in the areas of safety testing and accreditation, actuary or claims processing, as well as, cyber security and compliance.
So, these are just very broadly some of the roles that we have identified, but this would be an evolving journey and we hope to do this together with our transport workers.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I would just like to ask Senior Minister of State, how is our Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) participating in these trials and are there learning opportunities for students in our IHLs?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My second supplementary question is with regard to system-wide benefits, such as, accessibility, in particular.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For routes that are currently not viable, does the Ministry see that introduction of AVs create new opportunities for new routes?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: For example, night riders, bus services and if so, does the Ministry intend to run pilot trials for night rider bus services on AVs?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My last supplementary question is with regard to technology convergence with light rail systems.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, there are opportunities for us to work with IHLs when it comes to safety testing, as well as making sure that their curriculum looks into areas of AV technology to prepare them for when AV becomes more commonplace in our ecosystem.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They could be further away from the main transport nodes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On his last question, we will take a look at AV technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is evolving rapidly and we would remain open and see how we could use AV technology in as broad a range of transport vehicles as possible.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Can I just confirm that the framework also includes assessment on capability of the system under adverse weather conditions and also redundancy of system, in particular, for cybersecurity?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: My second question is, and the Senior Minister of State mentioned it earlier, AVs have the potential of helping us serve the quieter areas in towns.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: One possible area is the area in Jalan Loyang Besar.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Can the Senior Minister of State share a bit more about the timeline to scale up these pilots and how can we learn quickly and scale the use of AV in our towns?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: First and foremost, definitely, I think we are seeing quite extreme weather conditions happening all around the world and in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, the AV technology and what we are deploying on our roads is as tested, able to manage adverse weather conditions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the safety operators on board are also familiar with what to do, if there should be emergency situations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, that is the first phase, always with a safety operator on board.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The second stage we are inviting those who are interested to take the AVs to try out the technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It will be definitely safe by then, because the AVs would have been running around the roads for some time conducting mapping.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But apart from the technical performance indicators, what we are also doing through the pilot deployment is to socialise people to the idea of having the AVs on the road.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we are taking, really, a step by step approach to make sure that not only do we have the technical specifications, the performance indicators in place, that also our members of the public are socialised to the AVs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is why the roll-out is not as fast as some of us would like it to be, but we think that overall, this is safer and more acceptable to the public.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, after we do this pilot trial in deployment in Punggol, we are definitely thinking of rolling it out to more areas, and that is why I have shared about Tengah.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And if there are other suggestions from other Members in this House as to what are the other areas that we can roll this out in, we are more than happy to take in that feedback.
